key_insight: A stoichiometry-preserved ionic-cluster representation, paired with pretrained MLIP fine-tuning, can predict properties of multi-ionic energetic materials before full crystal structures are known.
engineering_relevance: This offers a synthesis-facing screening route for data-scarce materials design, reducing dependence on expensive crystal-structure prediction and enabling faster candidate prioritization.
method: Encode each candidate as a non-periodic stoichiometric ionic cluster instead of a periodic crystal.
Pretrain an atomistic backbone and fine-tune it with a multi-task energy–force objective to regularize sparse detonation labels.
Use the surrogate for cross-validated screening and extrapolation to new stoichiometries/cations without retraining.
evidence_signal: On 25 curated perovskite-type energetic materials with experimental detonation velocities, the approach achieved a mean absolute error of 92 m·s^-1 and correctly matched three newly synthesized ABX4 materials.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and diversity of the small labeled set, so extrapolation to very different chemistries or poorly represented stoichiometries should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
